signals.summary: A restorative, calm-movement wellness mood centered on evening wind-down and morning grounding rituals rather than hard training. Producible entirely as an empty mat, bolster, candle and morning/evening light in a quiet studio, no body required.
signals.why_now: Yoga With Adriene's catalogue leans hard into this restorative-ritual mood: 'Legs Up The Wall for Better Sleep' (623h), 'Sleep Better Tonight | 10-Minute Bedtime Flow' (1295h) and 'Start the Day Grounded | Morning Yoga' (959h). This is echoed by very fresh community interest, e.g. r/yoga 'I'm diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder... yoga changed that for me' (0.5h) and 'Could someone please tell me more about emotions during yoga?' (13.8h). A calm-ritual pairing across a major channel and live reddit interest.

signals.topic: Gentle movement & the 'doing less' walking trend
signals.summary: A cross-outlet shift away from high-intensity cardio toward low-intensity, gentle movement: walking, 'Zone 0', 'Japanese walking' and workouts built around doing almost nothing. Producible as trails, paths, walking shoes and serene outdoor/morning-light environments rather than exercising bodies.
signals.why_now: Multiple independent outlets frame the same wave: ELLE 'The New Workout Trend That Makes a Case for Doing Less' (2094h), WSJ 'I Tried the Workout That's All About Doing Almost Nothing' (3558h), nypost "'Zone 0' exercise is the 'extremely beneficial' fitness trend that 'doesn't feel like exercise'" (5381h), The Conversation 'From Japanese walking to 75 Hard' (3798h) and Men's Journal 'Forget Cardio and High Calorie Burns... a Major Shift in How We Think About Health' (1638h). Sources are aged but the low-effort-movement theme is evergreen and squarely on-brand.

signals.summary: A late-summer-into-autumn 'reset' moment as school and work routines resume, framed as calm, intentional wellbeing habits. Producible as cozy reset interiors: a tidy desk, journal, warm tea, morning light and a made-up mat/space rather than people.
signals.why_now: A back-to-routine cluster is timely for mid-August: DC News Now 'Mental wellness as school year begins' (109h), Hernando Sun 'Mind & Body: ...Practical Steps for Mental Wellness' (43h), and the recurring back-to-school framing in Harvard Health 'Helping Young People Maintain Mental Wellness During School Breaks' (1743h) plus 'Teen and youth mental wellness heading into new school year' (654h). Evidence skews to news/events, so treated as a seasonal mood cue rather than a hot viral wave.

signals.summary: A steady cross-outlet wave around daily mobility practice for freedom of movement and 'future-proofing' the body as you age. Producible only weakly, via mats, foam rollers and bands in a clean studio; the core subject is a moving body, which caps producibility.
signals.why_now: Several independent outlets carry the mobility theme: The Guardian 'how to start a mobility practice' (1302h), self.com '14 Mobility Moves Anyone Over 35 Should Add to Their Day' (3462h), Woman & Home "Dr Amir Khan's 3 mobility exercises to reduce stiffness" (147h) and Katie Couric Media 'Four Things That'll Keep You Strong, Steady, and Independent for Life' (1950h). Real and recurring, but body-dependent, so kept low despite good category fit.
